\section{What we did}

A fairness audit over three lending decisions --- consumer credit (German
Credit), mortgage origination (HMDA Georgia), peer-to-peer default risk (Lending
Club). A deterministic AIF360 layer computes every metric and assigns every
severity label by fixed rule; an LLM supplies only interpretation and is scored
against that ground truth. Audits run on the \textbf{full cleaned population}
(1{,}000 and 10{,}978 rows), not a test split: every row is scored out-of-fold by
a model that never saw it. Frozen prompts, a no-key replay path, two
anti-fabrication detectors, a \$15 cumulative cap. \textbf{Spend: \$0.8933 over
98 calls.} 60 tests, CI green.

\section{Five findings}

\textbf{1. The reporting floor erases the largest disparities.} An $n{\geq}15$
floor suppressed \textbf{5 of 11} HMDA \texttt{race}$\times$\texttt{sex} cells on
a test split. Three were worse than anything reported: the audit returned
\textsc{moderate} at $0.8169$ while the worst real disparity was $\mathbf{0.1917}$
--- wrong group, wrong by two severity bands. At full population 1 of 12 is
suppressed and the worst cell ($0.6734$) becomes visible. Every suppressed cell
belonged to a racial minority.

\textbf{2. The age audit used the wrong statute.} $40+$ is the ADEA, an
employment threshold; ECOA protects $62+$. Pooling young against senior
applicants cancels them, so banded \texttt{age\_group} reads $0.9791$
(\textsc{low}) while the statutory cut reads $\mathbf{0.8897}$ --- the largest age
disparity in the data. The \texttt{applicant\_age\_above\_62} flag was in the raw
file, unused.

\textbf{3. Metric orientation inverted a headline number.} UC3 \texttt{gender}
read $\mathrm{DI}=0.0$ (\textsc{critical}) because selection rates were computed
on the unfavorable label of a target named \texttt{loan\_default}. Correct value:
$0.9931$. Correct toolkit, clean data, sound metric, maximally wrong conclusion.

\textbf{4. Our own detectors penalised correct answers.} A refusal detector
flagged 6 responses, \emph{none} a refusal (any field under 40 characters counts
as empty, under a prompt demanding terseness). On a second provider it
mechanically zeroed 14 cycles, moving the mean from $\mathbf{70.0}$ to
$\mathbf{19.79}$ --- and a \emph{permanent block} was written into our config on
that evidence. Separately, a fabricated-metric detector flagged
\texttt{gpt-5-mini} 5$\times$ more often than \texttt{gpt-4o}, but
\textbf{67\%} of those flags are values derivable from the context ($88.88$ is
$0.8888$ as a percentage). The better-reasoning model is penalised for showing
its work.

\textbf{5. Three of our own published findings do not survive.} A
\textsc{critical} intersectional ratio of $0.6087$ becomes $\mathbf{0.8201}$ and
clears four-fifths once its \emph{15-person, 15/15} comparator grows to 69. An
inference about label bias came from a model with target leakage
(\texttt{interest\_rate}: 0.0\% missing on approvals, 99.3\% on denials; AUC
$0.9942 \rightarrow \mathbf{0.7915}$ once removed). And ``$0.8956$ fails the
$0.80$ screen'' is arithmetically false. UC3's \texttt{gender} is also
synthetic (\texttt{np.random.random} $>0.5$), so UC3 contains no protected class.

\section{Cross-model benchmark}

Same corrected packs, both models. \textbf{Prompt sensitivity is
model-generation-specific}: cycle-mean spread across four prompt strategies is
$14.7$ / $9.0$ points for \texttt{gpt-4o} (german\_credit / hmda) and
$\mathbf{0.0}$ / $\mathbf{1.9}$ for \texttt{gpt-5-mini}. The project's earlier
``prompt phrasing moves the verdict'' result reproduces on the older model and
nearly vanishes on the newer one. \texttt{gpt-5-mini} rejects \texttt{temperature}
outright, so a temperature sweep is impossible on it.
